q: 1. In residential buildings the height of bathroom should not be less than ...........
explain: Under building bylaws, bathrooms usually have a minimum height requirement of 2.4 meters.

q: 2. The nominal thickness of one-brick (un-plastered) wall is about ...........
explain: One-brick wall thickness is approximately 200 mm (including the mortar joint).

q: 3. The portion of wall on which the end of an arch rests is known as ...........
explain: The abutment is the masonry mass that supports the ends of an arch and resists its lateral thrust.

q: 4. The type of arch used for high class buildings where appearance is of prime importance, is known as ...........
explain: Gauged arches use bricks precisely cut to size and shape, allowing for very fine joints and a decorative look.

q: 5. A temporary structure to support an arch during construction is called ...........
explain: Centering is the temporary timber or steel framework that holds the bricks/stones of an arch in place until the mortar sets.

q: 6. A pointed arch which forms equilateral or isosceles triangle is known as ...........
explain: A lancet arch is a narrow, sharply pointed arch characteristic of Gothic architecture.

q: 7. Springers are those wedge shaped blocks of an arch which are provided at
explain: Springers are the first wedge-shaped units (voussoirs) placed at the ends of an arch, resting directly on the impost or the support (skewback) at the extremes.

q: 8. The perpendicular distance between intrados and extrados of an arch is called
explain: The depth of an arch is defined as the perpendicular distance between its inner curve (intrados) and its outer curve (extrados).
